en: to be harmless; to be innocuous

examples.en: This detergent is harmless to people.
It's a harmless bug, so don't worry.

examples.ko: 이 색소는 아이가 먹어도 무해하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this coloring is harmless even if a child eats it.

examples.ko: 무해하게 보이는 말이 상처가 될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Words that seem harmless can also hurt.
This plant is harmless even to dogs, so I feel relieved.

examples.ko: 무해하던 음식이 알레르기 때문에 위험해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Food that used to be harmless can become dangerous because of an allergy.

explain: 설명서, 뉴스, 제품 소개에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '괜찮아요'나 '안전해요'가 더 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '유해하다'예요.

phrases.en: Please give the baby only harmless food.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '무해한' when describing a noun that follows.

phrases.en: This chemical is not harmless to people.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form that softly says something is harmful.

phrases.en: This toy is safe for children.

explain_en: You often see it in manuals, the news, and product descriptions. In speech, '괜찮아요' or '안전해요' sounds more natural. Its opposite is '유해하다'.

en: to be insufficient; to be deficient

examples.ko: 자료가 불충분한 탓에 결론을 내리지 못했어요.
examples.en: Because the data was insufficient, we could not reach a conclusion.

examples.ko: 설명서가 불충분했기 때문에 조립하는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Because the instructions were inadequate, assembling it took a long time.

examples.ko: 잠이 불충분하면 낮에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you do not get enough sleep, you cannot concentrate during the day.
The preparation was not enough, so I postponed the presentation.
I realized in the match that my practice had not been enough.
If the explanation feels inadequate, please ask a question.

explain: '부족하다'와 비슷하지만 '불충분하다'는 기준에 못 미친다는 느낌이 있어서 설명, 자료, 준비, 증거에 잘 어울려요. 양이 모자랄 때는 '모자라다'도 써요. 반대는 '충분하다'예요.

phrases.example: 불충분한 증거로는 결론을 낼 수 없어요.
phrases.en: You can't reach a conclusion with insufficient evidence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증거, 자료, 설명 같은 말 앞에 자주 오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often placed before words like evidence, data, or explanation.

phrases.en: I prepared insufficiently, so the presentation was hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 준비가 기준에 못 미쳤다는 느낌을 부사형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form says that preparation fell short of the standard.

phrases.nuance_ko: '불충분하다'보다 부드럽고 일상 대화에서 더 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than '불충분하다' and more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: It is similar to '부족하다', but '불충분하다' suggests falling short of a standard, so it suits explanations, data, preparation, and evidence. For a simple shortage of amount, '모자라다' is also used. The opposite is '충분하다'.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 따뜻한 색조가 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like the warm tones of this painting.
I made the tone of the photo a bit darker.

examples.ko: 차분한 색조의 옷을 입고 면접을 봤어요.
examples.en: I wore clothes in calm tones to the interview.
I decorated the whole room in bright tones.
I went to the department store to buy color makeup.
The tones of the evening sky kept changing.

explain: '색깔'은 하나의 색, '색조'는 색들이 어울린 전체 분위기예요. 화장품 가게에서는 '색조 화장'이 립스틱·섀도처럼 색을 입히는 화장이라서 따로 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: I like paintings with calm color tones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색들이 만드는 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the mood made by the colors.

phrases.en: I wore light color makeup today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 립스틱, 섀도처럼 색을 입히는 화장을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means makeup that adds color, like lipstick and shadow.

phrases.nuance_ko: 영상이나 그림의 전체 색 분위기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the overall color mood of a film or picture.

explain_en: '색깔' is one color, while '색조' is the overall mood of colors working together. In a cosmetics shop, '색조 화장' means color makeup like lipstick and eyeshadow, so learn that separately.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 흥행은 못 했지만 작품성은 높아요.
examples.en: This film wasn't a box office hit, but its artistic quality is high.
It won a big award for its artistic merit.

examples.ko: 저는 작품성보다 재미를 먼저 따지는 편이에요.
examples.en: I tend to care about fun before artistic quality.
Critics rated it as having outstanding artistic quality.

examples.ko: 이 드라마는 작품성과 인기를 모두 잡았어요.
examples.en: This drama gained both artistic quality and popularity.
Please recommend a novel with artistic value.

explain: 영화, 소설, 그림 같은 작품을 예술적으로 얼마나 잘 만들었는지 말할 때 써요. '흥행성', '대중성'과 비교하며 '작품성은 좋은데 인기는 없다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I like movies with high artistic quality.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작품성'을 칭찬할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to praise a work's artistic quality.

phrases.example: 이 드라마는 인기는 많지만 작품성이 떨어져요.
phrases.en: This drama is popular, but its artistic quality is lacking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품이 예술적으로 아쉽다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a work falls short artistically.

phrases.en: It's a film with both artistic quality and mass appeal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 함께 놓고 비교하거나 칭찬할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to compare or praise both qualities together.

explain_en: It is used to talk about how well a film, novel or painting is made as art. It is often compared with '흥행성' and '대중성', as in '작품성은 좋은데 인기는 없다'.

examples.en: This storm is really destructive.
People were shocked by the earthquake's destructive power.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 공을 파괴력 있게 차요.
examples.en: That player kicks the ball with real force.
The impact of a rumor is much bigger than you think.

examples.ko: 새 기술이 시장에서 큰 파괴력을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The new technology showed great disruptive power in the market.
It was a weak typhoon, so the damage was small.

explain: 무기나 태풍처럼 부수는 힘에 쓰고, 스포츠나 소문처럼 상대를 크게 흔드는 힘에도 써요. 비슷한 '위력'은 좋은 일에도 쓰지만 '파괴력'은 부수고 흔드는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: This bomb has very strong destructive power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부수는 힘이 세다고 말할 때 써요. '파괴력이 크다'와 거의 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the destructive force is strong; almost the same as 파괴력이 크다.

phrases.example: 그 태풍은 엄청난 파괴력을 가지고 있어요.
phrases.en: That typhoon has enormous destructive power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 아주 클 때 앞에서 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before the noun to stress very great force.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 경기에서 무서운 파괴력을 보여 줬어요.
phrases.en: That player showed a frightening impact in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠에서 상대를 흔드는 힘을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used in sports for power that shakes the opponent.

explain_en: It is used for smashing power like weapons or typhoons, and also for strong influence such as in sports or rumors. The similar 위력 can describe good things too, while 파괴력 has a feel of breaking and shaking things.

examples.en: I did terribly on the exam, so I'm upset.

examples.ko: 어제 경기에서 우리 팀이 형편없이 졌어요.
examples.en: Our team lost badly in yesterday's game.
My cooking skills are awfully clumsy.
The service at that restaurant was terribly bad.
I got rained on, and my clothes got completely soaked.
I went to karaoke after a long time and sang terribly.

explain: '형편없다'의 부사형으로, 뒤에 '지다', '나쁘다', '서툴다'처럼 좋지 않은 말이 자주 와요. '엉망으로'와 비슷하지만 수준이 매우 낮다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 명사 앞에서는 '형편없는'을 써요.

phrases.en: My cooking skills are pretty terrible.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, change it to 'hyeongpyeoneopsneun'.

phrases.en: My score on this test is terribly low.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낮다'처럼 수준이 좋지 않다는 말과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with words about a poor level, like 'nat-da'.

phrases.en: Today's game result is really awful.

explain_en: This is the adverb form of '형편없다', and it is often followed by negative words like '지다' (lose), '나쁘다', and '서툴다'. It resembles '엉망으로' (in a mess), but feels more like the level is extremely low. Before a noun, use '형편없는'.
